# nxos_sla (Resource)

This resource can manage the IP SLA configuration on NX-OS devices, including sender probes (ICMP echo, UDP echo, UDP jitter, TCP connect, DNS and HTTP operations), reactions, schedules, group schedules, responder, TWAMP responder and TWAMP server settings.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "nxos_sla" "example" {
  sender_logging_level = 5
  sender_logging_traps = true
  probes = {
    "1" = {
      icmp_echo_buckets_kept                     = 30
      icmp_echo_destination_ip                   = "10.1.1.1"
      icmp_echo_distributions_of_statistics_kept = 5
      icmp_echo_enhanced_buckets                 = 50
      icmp_echo_enhanced_interval                = 900
      icmp_echo_filter                           = "All"
      icmp_echo_frequency                        = 30
      icmp_echo_hours_of_statistics_kept         = 5
      icmp_echo_tos                              = 10
      icmp_echo_lives_kept                       = 1
      icmp_echo_owner                            = "OWNER1"
      icmp_echo_request_data_size                = 100
      icmp_echo_source_interface                 = "eth1/10"
      icmp_echo_statistics_distribution_interval = 10
      icmp_echo_tag                              = "TAG1"
      icmp_echo_threshold                        = 1000
      icmp_echo_timeout                          = 2000
      icmp_echo_verify_data                      = true
      icmp_echo_vrf                              = "management"
      reactions = {
        "rtt" = {
          lower_threshold   = 1000
          reaction_type     = "trapAndTrigger"
          threshold_count_x = 3
          threshold_count_y = 10
          threshold_type    = "xOfy"
          upper_threshold   = 2000
        }
      }
      reaction_triggers = {
        "2" = {}
      }
      schedule_age_out     = 86400
      schedule_life        = 7200
      schedule_recurring   = true
      schedule_start_probe = "At"
      schedule_start_time  = "10:00:00"
    }
  }
  group_schedules = {
    "1" = {
      age_out         = 3600
      frequency       = 30
      life            = 7200
      probe_list      = "3"
      schedule_period = 10
      start_probe     = "After"
      start_time      = "01:00:00"
    }
  }
  responder_admin_state   = true
  responder_logging_level = 5
  permanent_responders = {
    "udp;5000;10.1.1.1" = {}
  }
  twamp_responder_admin_state   = true
  twamp_responder_timeout       = 600
  twamp_server_admin_state      = true
  twamp_server_inactivity_timer = 600
  twamp_server_logging_level    = 5
  twamp_server_port             = 5862
}
```

## Schema

### Optional

- `deletion_policy` (String) What happens on the device when objects managed by the resource are removed. `delete` deletes the object on destroy, including any configuration not managed by Terraform, and deletes single child objects once none of their attributes are configured anymore, unless the device holds other entries below them. `reset` deletes the objects created by the resource on destroy, resets the managed attributes of the objects that already existed and leaves configuration not managed by Terraform in place. `retain` leaves the device unchanged on destroy and only removes the resource from the state. Overrides the `deletion_policy` of the provider, which defaults to `delete`. See the [Deletion Policy](../guides/deletion_policy) guide for details.
  - Choices: `delete`, `reset`, `retain`
- `device` (String) A device name from the provider configuration.
- `group_schedules` (Attributes Map) List of IP SLA group schedules.
  - Map key: `id` - Group scheduler index.
  - Key range: `1`-`65535` (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--group_schedules))
- `permanent_responders` (Attributes Map) List of permanent responders.
  - Map key format: `<protocol>;<port>;<ip_address>`
  - Key component `protocol`: Responder protocol types supported types are udp-echo, tcp-connect. Choices: `udp`, `tcp`.
  - Key component `port`: Port on which the responder is listenening to receive the packets from the sender. This property is applicable only for TCP or UDP protocol. Required only if ip sla sender probe's control is disabled. Permanently enables the responder functionality on the specified port. Range: `1`-`65535`.
  - Key component `ip_address`: IP on which the responder is listenening to receive the packets from the sender. This property is applicable only for TCP or UDP protocol. Required only if ip sla sender probe's control is disabled. Permanently enables the responder functionality on the specified port and IP. If the user needs wild card IP address, then use 0.0.0.0(any IP). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--permanent_responders))
- `probes` (Attributes Map) List of IP SLA probes (operations).
  - Map key: `id` - Operation index which is unique for each probe, all the probe related configs and the statistics are displayed using this index.
  - Key range: `1`-`2147483647` (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--probes))
- `responder_admin_state` (Boolean) Enable or disable the ip sla responder. To enable responder, feature sla responder is to be enabled.
- `responder_logging_level` (Number) configures the logging level for ip sla responder. The property can be set only if feature sla responder is enabled.
  - Range: `0`-`7`
- `sender_logging_level` (Number) configures the logging level for ip sla sender. The property can be set only if feature sla sender is enabled.
  - Range: `0`-`7`
- `sender_logging_traps` (Boolean) Enable syslog traps which sends the trap meesages on reaction-config trap is enabled.
- `sender_reset` (Boolean) Resets all sla probe related configuration.
- `twamp_responder_admin_state` (Boolean) Enable or disable the twamp responder. To enable twamp responder, feature sla responder is to be enabled.
- `twamp_responder_timeout` (Number) TWAMP Responder Session inactivity timeout in seconds (default 900).
  - Range: `1`-`604800`
- `twamp_server_admin_state` (Boolean) Enable or disable the ip sla twamp server. To enable twamp-server, feature sla twamp-server is to be enabled.
- `twamp_server_inactivity_timer` (Number) TWAMP Server Inactivity Timer, Max number of inactive seconds (default 900).
  - Range: `1`-`6000`
- `twamp_server_logging_level` (Number) configures the logging level for twamp server. The property can be set only if feature sla twamp-server is enabled.
  - Range: `0`-`7`
- `twamp_server_port` (Number) TWAMP Server Port on which the TCP control connection is established.(default 862).
  - Range: `1`-`65535`

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The distinguished name of the object.

<a id="nestedatt--group_schedules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `group_schedules`

Optional:

- `age_out` (Number) How long to keep the probes, when inactive (in seconds).
  - Range: `0`-`2073600`
- `day_of_month` (Number) At which day of the configured month, the probe is to be started.Setting the value as zero means current day of the time. This property is applicable only when the startProbe proeprty is set as At.
  - Range: `0`-`31`
- `frequency` (Number) Group operation frequency (in seconds) using which the probes are scheduled.
  - Range: `1`-`604800`
- `frequency_range` (String) Group operation frequency (in seconds) either in range as x-y, frequency-range is used for random scheduling.
- `life` (Number) Length of time to execute in seconds.
  - Range: `0`-`2147483647`
- `modify_group_schedule` (String) modify the existing group schedule.
  - Choices: `create`, `add`, `delete`
- `month` (String) At which month, the probe is to be started. This property is applicable only when the startProbe proeprty is set as At.
  - Choices: `None`, `January`, `February`, `March`, `April`, `May`, `June`, `July`, `August`, `September`, `October`, `November`, `December`
- `probe_list` (String) Multiple probe ID's to be group scheduled, List of one or more identification(ID) numbers of the IP SLAs operations to be included in a new multioperation schedule. (Max up to 125 characters). Indicate ranges of operation ID numbers with a hyphen. Individual ID numbers and ranges of ID numbers are delimited by a comma. For example, enter a list of operation ID numbers in any of the following ways: x-y,a-b,c-f or x,y,a,b,c,f or x-y,a,b,c-f.
- `reschedule` (Boolean) Restarting a scheduled probe.
- `schedule_period` (Number) Group schedule period in seconds, This is the time period in which the group of the probes configured in probeList are scheduled at an equal gap between them.
  - Range: `0`-`604800`
- `start_probe` (String) When the probe is to be started.
  - Choices: `Now`, `At`, `Pending`, `After`
- `start_time` (String) When to start this probe on a given day and month in Hour(s):Minute(s):Second(s) i.e in (H:M:S) format. This property is applicable only when the startProbe proeprty is set as At or After.

### Nested Schema for `probes`

Optional:

- `dns_buckets_kept` (Number) Bucket size value - Maximum number of history buckets to collect.
  - Range: `1`-`60`
- `dns_distributions_of_statistics_kept` (Number) Maximum number of statistics distribution buckets to capture.
  - Range: `1`-`20`
- `dns_filter` (String) Bucket size value - Maximum number of history buckets to collect.
  - Choices: `None`, `All`, `OverThreshold`, `Failures`
- `dns_frequency` (Number) Frequency of an operation - The interval at which the configured destination is tracked by the probe. Frequency in seconds(default value is 60). Minimum frequency value for an IP SLAs HTTP probe operation is 60 seconds but 1 second for other probes.
  - Range: `1`-`604800`
- `dns_hours_of_statistics_kept` (Number) Maximum number of statistics hour groups to capture.
  - Range: `0`-`25`
- `dns_lives_kept` (Number) Maximum number of history lives to collect.
  - Range: `0`-`2`
- `dns_name_server_hostname` (String) Host name of the name server, from which the DNS name server IP address is resolved. Name server IP address which is used to resolve the target host name or target host ip configured in the probe. This property is applicable only incase of DNS probe.
- `dns_name_server_ip` (String) Name server IP address which is used to resolve the target host name or target host ip configured in the probe.This property is applicable only if the configured probe type is DNS.
- `dns_owner` (String) Owner string of the probe(Max size 127).
- `dns_source_hostname` (String) Source Host Name, if IP address is resolved from DNS server. Modifying this property is not allowed.
- `dns_source_ip` (String) Source`IP address from which the configured destination is tracked by the probe. Modifying this property is not allowed.
- `dns_source_port` (Number) Source Port configuration for DNS probe.
  - Range: `0`-`4294967295`
- `dns_statistics_distribution_interval` (Number) Statistics distribution interval size, if the precision configured is in milliseconds, then the unit is in milliseconds else if it is microseconds, then the unit is in microseconds.
  - Range: `1`-`100000`
- `dns_tag` (String) User defined tag string (Max Size 127).
- `dns_target` (String) This property can be either Host name or IP address (IPv4 address format x.x.x.x),(no IPv6 support) for which the resolution happens either by name or by IP to name respectively, in the configured probe. This property is applicable only incase of DNS probe.
- `dns_threshold` (Number) Operation threshold - this is an upper limit for the observed RTT for the probe. RTT value of a probe exceeding the configured threshold will be marked with Overthreshold return code.
  - Range: `1`-`60000`
- `dns_timeout` (Number) Timeout of an operation - this is the maximum wait time for completing the operation. The probe will be marked with Timeout return code.
  - Range: `1`-`604800000`
- `dns_vrf` (String) vrf on which the probe is configured.
- `http_buckets_kept` (Number) Bucket size value - Maximum number of history buckets to collect.
  - Range: `1`-`60`
- `http_cache` (Boolean) The config to enable/disable the download of cached HTTP page.

  - Range: `1`-`20`
- `http_filter` (String) Bucket size value - Maximum number of history buckets to collect.
  - Choices: `None`, `All`, `OverThreshold`, `Failures`
- `http_frequency` (Number) Operation frequency (in seconds) using which the probes are scheduled.
  - Range: `60`-`604800`
- `http_hours_of_statistics_kept` (Number) Maximum number of statistics hour groups to capture.
  - Range: `0`-`25`
- `http_ipv6_traffic_class` (Number) TOS if the probe is tracking IPv4 destination and Traffic Class if the probe is tracking IPv6 destination.
  - Range: `0`-`4294967295`
- `http_lives_kept` (Number) Maximum number of history lives to collect.
  - Range: `0`-`2`
- `http_method` (String) HTTP method - Currently only the get method is supported.For GET requests,IP SLAs will format the request based on the specified http URL.
  - Choices: `get`

- `http_proxy` (String) Proxy information - proxy URL.

  - Range: `1`-`100000`

  - Range: `1`-`60000`
- `http_timeout` (Number) Timeout of an operation - this is the maximum wait time for completing the operation. The probe will be marked with Timeout return code.

<a id="nestedatt--probes--reaction_triggers"></a>
### Nested Schema for `probes.reaction_triggers`


<a id="nestedatt--probes--reactions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `probes.reactions`

Optional:

- `lower_threshold` (Number) Lower limit for Threshold.
  - Range: `1`-`60000`
- `reaction_type` (String) The config is to notify the user when the monitored performance parameter value rises above or falls below a specified threshold. The notification can be either as SNMP traps or trigger to a new probe.
  - Choices: `none`, `trapOnly`, `triggerOnly`, `trapAndTrigger`
- `threshold_count_x` (Number) The config denotes the number of times the monitored performance parameter value rises above or falls below a specified threshold. This config applies only for the thresholdType 1. average 2. consecutive 3. xOfy.
  - Range: `1`-`16`
- `threshold_count_y` (Number) The config denotes the number of times the monitored performance parameter value rises above or falls below a specified threshold. This config applies only for the thresholdType xOfy.
  - Range: `1`-`16`
- `threshold_type` (String) The config says when the configured reactionType should be triggered.
  - Choices: `never`, `immediate`, `consecutive`, `xOfy`, `average`
- `upper_threshold` (Number) Upper limit for Threshold.
  - Range: `1`-`60000`

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to       = nxos_sla.example
  identity = {}
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema


#### Optional

- `device` (String) A device name from the provider configuration.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
# Terraform's `import` block requires a non-empty `id` value, so this format cannot be used to
# import nxos_sla for the default device. Use the `terraform import` command
# below, or identity-based import shown above, instead.
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import nxos_sla.example ""
```
